topic: Microsoft's AI Revenue Mostly Comes from OpenAI: What the Disclosures Reveal 2026

That's roughly 70% of Microsoft's total AI business
CEO Nadella said AI business on track to top $37B annually
OpenAI pays Microsoft for computing power, model development costs, and revenue share
Reliance explains Microsoft's recent championing of open-weight models

stats.fact: Microsoft recorded $24.1 billion in revenue from commercial arrangements with OpenAI in fiscal 2026
OpenAI-related revenue represents approximately 70% of Microsoft's total AI business
CEO Satya Nadella said Microsoft's AI business was on track to exceed $37 billion annually (March 2026)
Microsoft reported $6 billion in accounts receivable from OpenAI as of June 30, 2026
Microsoft has invested approximately $12 billion in OpenAI since 2019
Microsoft committed a total of $13 billion to OpenAI, with $11.9 billion funded as of June 30, 2026
OpenAI committed to purchase an additional $250 billion in Azure services under revised agreement
Microsoft's stake in OpenAI was reduced to 27% (valued at $135 billion) during October 2025 restructuring
Microsoft held a 32.5% stake in OpenAI before the October 2025 restructuring
In April 2026, Microsoft and OpenAI amended partnership allowing OpenAI to offer products across any cloud provider

angles: Microsoft's OpenAI dependency reveals a strategic vulnerability — 70% reliance on a single partner for AI revenue
The disclosure explains Microsoft's sudden shift toward open-weight models and anti-proprietary rhetoric
Despite $250B Azure commitment from OpenAI, the multi-cloud shift (Amazon investment) signals OpenAI's independence play
Microsoft's $12B investment in OpenAI has yielded massive returns, but the reduced stake (32.5% → 27%) shows dilution risk
The lack of breakdown in the $24.1B figure (Azure vs. revenue-share vs. other) leaves room for interpretation and speculation
Microsoft's AI revenue concentration risk: what happens if OpenAI develops its own cloud infrastructure or shifts further to AWS?
The disclosure timing — post-OpenAI restructuring and Amazon investment — suggests Microsoft is managing investor expectations
